# Non-issues

Findings without a valid failing Go test: found by code reading, preconditions etcd meets, documentation, behavior etcd does not guarantee ([../issues/README.md](../issues/README.md), "A non-issue").

| Finding | Why not an issue | Blocks proof | Upstream |
|---|---|---|---|
| [bbolt: `CreateBucket` accepts bucket names longer than `MaxKeySize`, though documented to refuse them](bbolt-bucket-name-length-unchecked.md) | documentation only, and a length etcd never uses: etcd's bucket names are a few bytes (`server/storage/schema/bucket.go`). Either the documentation should drop "too long" or the functions should return `ErrKeyTooLarge` (or a bucket-specific error) above `MaxKeySize`. A name large enough to make the root's leaf page exceed `MaxAllocSize` would hit the same panic as `issues/bbolt-max-value-size-unusable.md`. | no | none |
| [bbolt: a commit that succeeds after a failed sync can leave a database a crash corrupts](bbolt-commit-after-failed-sync.md) | a precondition etcd meets: etcd exits on any commit error (`server/storage/backend/batch_tx.go:302`, `lg.Fatal`) and syncs only its defragmentation copy, fatally on an error (`backend.go:578-581`); bbolt documents nothing about continuing after a sync error, and the general answer (PostgreSQL's "fsyncgate", 2018) is that an fsync error must be treated as fatal for the data written since the last good sync. No test here: it needs fault injection in `fdatasync` and a crash (found by reasoning about OsFs's model of a failed sync, D2 of `notes/osfs-ext-plan.md`, which follows Linux). | no | none |
| [bbolt: a database file Open creates is never made durable in its directory](bbolt-create-dir-not-synced.md) | behavior etcd does not observe in practice: on journaled ext4 (`data=ordered`, the default) and on xfs, an `fsync`/`fdatasync` of a newly created file commits the journal transaction that created its directory entry, so the name survives with the file's first synced commit. etcd's directories are created by `fileutil.TouchDirAll` (`server/etcdserver/bootstrap.go:64-68, 211`), which syncs nothing (`os.MkdirAll` and a written and removed `.touch` file, `client/pkg/v3/fileutil/fileutil.go:36-68`), so etcd relies on the same file system behavior for its member directory too (`etcd-member-dir-not-synced.md`, found 2026-11-09). Other file systems (and POSIX as written) do not promise it. No test here: it needs a crash simulation of the directory (found by reading OsFs's model, D4 of `notes/osfs-ext-plan.md`, where a created file's name is not durable until its directory is synced). A first boot whose database vanishes is recovered by etcd from its WAL (the consistent index restarts at 0), so etcd's correctness does not rest on it, but only before the member's first local snapshot: after one, the restart panics (`etcd-backend-name-lost-restart-panic.md`, found 2026-11-09). | no | none |
| [bbolt: `Cursor.Prev` after the end depends on how the end was reached](bbolt-cursor-prev-after-next-end.md) | documentation and API behavior, not a reachable failure in etcd: etcd's backend never calls `Prev` (its ranges are `Seek` then `Next`). The doc of `Next`/`Prev` could state where the cursor stays, or `next` could step past the last element as `Seek` does. | no | none |
| [bbolt: `DeleteBucket` of the empty name reports an incompatible value in an empty database](bbolt-deletebucket-empty-name.md) | a wrong error value only, on a name no bucket can have; etcd's backend never deletes a bucket by the empty name. Cause: the cursor's `seek` of `""` in an empty root bucket returns a nil key, and `bytes.Equal([]byte{}, nil)` is true, so `DeleteBucket` takes the nil entry (flags `0`) for a found key that is not a bucket. | no | none |
| [bbolt: a bucket handle used after its bucket is deleted panics or silently misses the data](bbolt-deleted-bucket-handle.md) | a precondition etcd meets and documentation only: etcd's backend looks the bucket up by name for every operation (`server/storage/backend/batch_tx.go`, `read_tx.go`), so no handle outlives a `DeleteBucket`; using a handle to a deleted bucket is a use most bbolt users would call a mistake, and the fix is a sentence on `Tx.Bucket`/`DeleteBucket` (or an `ErrBucketNotFound` from the handle's methods). | no | none |
| [bbolt: after a failed remap, the next transaction would dereference a nil meta page](bbolt-failed-remap-nil-meta-panic.md) | fixed in bbolt since v1.3.7 (bbolt#362): `beginTx` and `beginRWTx` check `db.data == nil` under `mmaplock` and return `ErrInvalidMapping`, so v1.5.0 (etcd's) returns an error. The panic was only in this repository's minibolt (`examples/osfs/bboltfs/minibolt.go`), which copied the remap without that check; and etcd stops on any failed commit anyway. | no | fixed |
| [bbolt: a NaN `Bucket.FillPercent` makes `Commit` panic (amd64)](bbolt-fillpercent-nan.md) | a precondition etcd meets: `FillPercent` is a ratio, and etcd sets only `0.9` (`server/storage/backend/batch_tx.go`, `backend.go`); a NaN fill percent is a caller bug. | no | none |
| [bbolt: with both meta pages unreadable or damaged, `Open` can take the page size from a user value](bbolt-getpagesize-probes-user-data.md) | a hardening finding that needs a double fault, found by code reading: - **Two faults.** A single fault is caught by the second meta page: if one meta read fails or one meta is torn, the other is valid and the probe stops at offset 4096. bbolt writes one meta per commit, alternating between the pages, so a normal crash damages at most one. - **No longer reachable through read errors on the fork.** The goose fork returns a meta read error instead of probing past it. There, only two checksum-invalid metas reach user pages: a double corruption, in which `Open` cannot be correct anyway, but should fail rather than pick a user value's fake meta. - **Not etcd's case.** etcd's values are client data, so a forged meta inside a value is possible. But the double fault is a media failure or a corrupted file. | no | none |

| [etcdserver: the snapshot-database purge deletes a received snapshot's `.snap.db` that the apply loop has not opened yet](etcd-purge-snapdb-unopened.md) | no test reaches it the way etcd runs: the test stages the six files directly (as rafthttp's snapshot handler saves them) and drives `raftNode` with the package's fake raft node. The other files the purge counts are orphans: `MsgSnap`s rafthttp saved but raft ignored (a stale term, an index at or below the commit index) or files left by a crash between `SaveDBFrom` and the raft loop's persistence; reaching five of them above a pending snapshot takes leader changes, partitions or crashes in an order not excluded by any check but not shown possible either. | [raft: with the initial configuration only in an index-0 snapshot, a node added later can win an election alone](raft-joiner-empty-confstate.md) | a precondition of how an application bootstraps a cluster, which etcd and raft's documented paths meet: a new etcd cluster starts with `StartNode` and peers (`server/etcdserver/bootstrap.go`), so the initial configuration is in the log; the README starts a cluster the same way, and `RawNode.Bootstrap`'s doc recommends a manual bootstrap with first index > 1, where a joiner is caught up by snapshot. The index-0 snapshot of etcd-io/raft#370 is used by etcd only at restart, when the log still holds the conf entries. At most worth documenting (the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Nonissue, maybe some documentation would help"). | no | none |
| [raft: an empty `ConfChangeV2` with a joint transition, proposed in a joint config, panics every node that applies it](raft-joint-empty-transition-panic.md) | reaching it takes a proposal the documentation does not describe: `raft.proto` documents leaving a joint configuration as "proposing a ConfChangeV2 with only and optionally the Context field populated" (the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "the bad execution requires violating the raft documentation's instructions"); etcd proposes only v1 `ConfChange`s and never enters a joint configuration. | no | none |
| [raft: a read at a leader that alone is a quorum of a joint configuration waits for a learner's heartbeat response](raft-joint-self-quorum-read.md) | not a guarantee raft makes (no bound on when a read is answered; it is answered as soon as the learner responds), in a configuration etcd never enters (etcd proposes only v1 conf changes, never joint ones), and a read retried after the joint state is answered at once; The 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Skip for now". | no | none |
| [raft: `MemoryStorage.CreateSnapshot` panics outside an undocumented index range](raft-memorystorage-createsnapshot-bounds.md) | a precondition etcd meets (it calls `CreateSnapshot` only with its applied index, after the entries are persisted, and compacts only below its last snapshot); documentation only (the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Skip for now"). | no | none |
| [raft: `MemoryStorage`'s mutex comment names only `Append` as the application's, but every writer is](raft-memorystorage-mutex-comment.md) | documentation only, no bug: the mutex does protect every `MemoryStorage` method that writes (`InitialState`'s unlocked read is [`raft-memorystorage-initialstate-unlocked`](../issues/raft-memorystorage-initialstate-unlocked.md)). | no | none |
| [raft: a stepped `MsgApp`'s entries slice is adopted, so its spare capacity must belong to the receiver](raft-msgapp-inprocess-aliasing.md) | a precondition etcd meets, found by code reading, no test. rafthttp gives the receiver a fresh decode of every message (protobuf's unmarshalling allocates the slice), and raft's own `MsgApp`s carry slices with no spare capacity: `raftLog.slice` clips what it returns ([log.go:510](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/b867cf13/log.go#L507-L510); the mixed path allocates exactly in `extend`), provided the `Storage`'s `Entries` protects its array as its documentation asks (`MemoryStorage` returns `ents[:len(ents):len(ents)]`, [storage.go:165](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/b867cf13/storage.go#L161-L165)). The hazard needs an in-process transport stepping a message with spare capacity it does not own: a `Storage` that breaks the documented `Entries` contract, or a hand-built `MsgApp`. raft's documentation does not say that `Step` may keep and append to the message's entries slice. | no | none |
| [raft: a pre-candidate counts a pre-vote granted in an earlier pre-campaign](raft-prevote-stale-grant.md) | not a guarantee raft makes: discussed upstream in 2017 (etcd-io/etcd#8288) and accepted as a rare false positive that costs one election, not safety; the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "non-issue, based on the prior discussion; would want to see problems demonstrated to revisit". | no | known |
| [raft v3.7: `node.run` reads `Ready.Messages` responses after handing the `Ready` out](raft-ready-messages-read-after-handout.md) | no test (code reading); a precondition etcd meets (v3.7's `processMessages` only reads the messages); at most worth documenting (the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Nonissue; maybe some docs"). | no | none |
| [raft: a conf change removing the last voter is committed, then panics every node that applies it](raft-remove-last-voter-panic.md) | the panic only replaces the loss of the cluster the operator asked for (a cluster whose last voter is removed cannot make progress either way), and etcd refuses the request by default: `mayRemoveMember` rejects removing the only voting member unless `--strict-reconfig-check=false` (server/etcdserver/server.go; `IsReadyToRemoveVotingMember`); The 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Skip for now" ("a self-inflicted loss of the cluster"). | no | none |
| [raft: `Node.ReportSnapshot`'s comment says `SnapshotFinish` is a no-op; without it a leader can stay paused on a follower](raft-reportsnapshot-finish-not-noop.md) | documentation only, contradicted by the other raft docs (doc.go: "call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent"; `Ready.Messages`: "MUST report back to raft when the snapshot has been received or has failed"); etcd always reports `SnapshotFinish` after an upload, and the comment's fix is in etcd-io/raft#243. | no | known |
| [raft: a node restarted from a malformed `ConfState` panics in `newRaft`](raft-restore-malformed-confstate-panic.md) | a malformed storage input, found by code reading, no test: the `ConfState`s etcd stores come from raft (`ApplyConfChange`), which produces neither form. | [raft: a member added after the storage's latest snapshot is sent that snapshot forever](raft-snapshot-without-recipient-livelock.md) | an unstated precondition on what the storage's snapshot covers (that it includes every member the leader may send it to), which etcd meets: it replaces the metadata of every snapshot raft sends by its applied index and configuration (`createMergedSnapshotMessage(m, ep.appliedt, ep.appliedi, ep.confState)`, [server/etcdserver/server.go](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/a2e3642bcd2cca3a802503cdb09f64a3dc15cdf5/server/etcdserver/server.go#L995)), so the snapshot a newcomer receives always includes it; and liveness only. Raft's [`Storage.Snapshot`](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/c51f010c851edd0dada5af41bafbf68e54617767/storage.go#L91-L95) says only "the most recent snapshot", while [`restore`](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/c51f010c851edd0dada5af41bafbf68e54617767/raft.go#L1869-L1898) drops one without the recipient ("should never happen") and [`maybeSendSnapshot`](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/c51f010c851edd0dada5af41bafbf68e54617767/raft.go#L666-L681) sends it regardless. The same kind of documentation gap as [`raft-compact-past-snapshot`](raft-compact-past-snapshot.md). | no | none |
| [raft: `StartNode` on a non-empty storage only logs a warning and runs the node as a restart](raft-startnode-nonempty-storage-silent-restart.md) | documentation only, and a precondition etcd meets: etcd calls `StartNode` only with peers, which it has only at the first start of a new cluster, with no WAL, on a fresh `MemoryStorage` (`server/etcdserver/bootstrap.go`, `bootstrapRaft`: `!haveWAL && cfg.NewCluster`); every other start calls `RestartNode`. The doc comment could say that the storage must be empty, or `StartNode` could fail instead of warning. Found by code reading; no test. | no | none |
| [raft v3.7: `Step` writes into the caller's message and keeps it](raft-step-writes-caller-message.md) | documentation only: `Step`'s comment already forbids the caller from touching `m` afterwards, and etcd steps freshly decoded messages it does not reuse (the 2026-10-23 review's Plan: "Non-issue, maybe some documentation change"). | no | none |
| [raft: reads postponed until a new leader's first commit are not released when a configuration change makes that commit](raft-switchtoconfig-pending-reads.md) | no test, found by code reading, and unreachable under doc.go's protocol: a conf change applied at a leader was either committed before its term (then applied before the election, as `hup` refuses to campaign with unapplied conf changes) or in its term (then the leader had already committed in its term through `MsgAppResp`, which released the reads).
